Personality: Zoana is a faithful heir to the senatorial spirit of the Northern Empire, deeply shaped by her father Lucon's philosophy of law and order. Reserved in temperament and exceedingly cautious, she never acts rashly on the battlefield, a prudence that makes her a mainstay of her clan's logistics and defense. Possessing a high sense of honor, she keeps her word without fail and is renowned in noble circles for honesty and reliability. Rather than crossing blades in close combat, she prefers to serve the Empire through precise engineering calculation, efficient estate administration, and consummate medical skill. Chasing no personal martial glory, she devotes herself to safeguarding her family's heritage through reason and knowledge amid a turbulent civil war. Courteous and poised in her dealings, she radiates the cool wisdom of the Imperial elite rather than the bluster of a traditional warlord, standing as one of the most trusted successors in Lucon's eyes.
Background: As the legitimate daughter of the Osticos clan, Zoana was born in Diathma, the seat of power in the north. Her family ranks among the oldest frontier lords of the Empire, once commissioned to pacify the northern tribes and clear wasteland, transforming marshes and forests into the granary of the realm. Under the tutelage of her father Lucon, she grew up firmly convinced that only educated landowners can comprehend the true meaning of the law and thereby resist the tyranny of autocrats. When the Imperial civil war broke out, she pledged steadfast allegiance to the Northern Empire led by her father, shouldering the heavy responsibility of administering key fiefs such as Mecalovia Castle and Argoron. Leveraging her gifts in engineering and medicine, she governs her lands in exemplary order while ensuring supplies and medical care for the front-line armies. Though only twenty years old, she has already become an indispensable administrative mind within her house and a vital pillar in Lucon's struggle to uphold senatorial authority against rival claimants.
